findings.detail: references test files 'tests/'
Implements routine 'localize-patch' that suggests and applies a source-code patch when a test failure's traceback points only at test files.
Limits itself to 3 attempts, tracked in state.notes['lp_tries'].
Only runs after routine 'ask-student' has run at least 3 times.
Filters failures to those whose traceback frames contain no non-test file ('blind' failures).
Treats paths starting with 'tests/' or 'test_' as test files.
Extracts the test file path from traceback frames.
Parses 'import' and 'from ... import' lines from the failing test to infer candidate source modules.
Maps imported module names to files in state.files, including .py and __init__.py matches, capped at 4 candidates.
Reads the failing test file and up to 70 lines of each candidate source file.
Builds a prompt asking student.ask('patch', ...) to choose a candidate file and give a verbatim search/replace block, with instruction never to edit tests/.
Calls student.ask, which may perform an external model/service/network call depending on the student implementation.
Locates the real target by checking which candidate file contains the student-provided search string.
Restricts the edit target to candidate files or the located file.
Calls tools.edit_file(target, search, replace) to modify source code.
Calls tools.run_tests() before and after the edit and records pass/fail counts.
Marks state.done when the suite passes after patching.
If the post-patch failure count increases, attempts to revert by calling tools.edit_file(target, replace, search) and marks the patch reverted.
Appends patch records to state.patches.
Reads and edits file paths supplied via state.failures, state.files, and student output without restricting them to the working directory.
Executes the project's test suite through tools.run_tests(), i.e., process/code execution of repository tests.
Does not directly read environment variables, credentials, secrets, open network sockets, use subprocess, or use eval/exec in the shown code.
